item.title: Microsoft security advisory – August 2026 monthly rollup (AV26-804)
New CISO appointments 2026
item.description:
The upper ranks of corporate security are seeing a high rate of change as companies try to adapt to the evolving threat landscape. Many companies are hiring a chief security officer (CSO) or chief information security officer (CISO) for the first time to support a deeper commitment to information security.

Follow this column to keep up with new appointments to senior-level security roles and perhaps gain a little insight into hiring trends. If you have an announcement of your own that you would like us to include here, contact Peter Sayer, executive editor of news, at peter_sayer@foundryco.com.

New CISO appointments in August 2026

Erika Dean named CISO at Tricentis

Tricentis appointed Erika Dean its CISO. Dean’s cybersecurity leadership career spans financial services and technology, including appointments leading security programs at Robinhood and Capital One, where she focused on protecting organizations while enabling business growth and strengthening operational resilience.

Todd Dekkinga joins Sycomp as security chief

Sycomp appointed Todd Dekkinga as CISO to lead the company’s growing security practice. Dekkinga brings extensive experience as a cybersecurity and risk management executive and has held IT leadership and advisory roles in technology, financial services, and life sciences.

New CISO appointments in July 2026

US Department of Energy appoints new CESER director

The US DoE tapped Andrew McClure to be its new Director of the Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response. McClure brings over a decade of experience at Forgepoint Capital focusing on cybersecurity and infrastructure. He previously served in the US Marine Corps as an intelligence officer.

Dallas names James Wilkinson as CISO

The City of Dallas appointed James L. Wilkinson as chief information security officer. Wilkinson is a 25-year industry veteran with experience spanning national security, financial services, aerospace, and defense. He began his career with the US Army and US Marine Corps, including serving as Chief of Cyber Mission Forces, and later held senior positions at Wells Fargo, Lockheed Martin, and MUFG Bank.

Alexander Truskovsky promoted to CISO at EigenQ

EigenQ elevated Alexander Truskovsky to chief information security officer, a newly established position following his tenure as VP of Cryptography. Truskovsky will lead IS strategy, cybersecurity governance, and security architecture. He brings expertise as an accomplished inventor, cryptography leader, and enterprise solutions architect.

PNC names Christian Winward CISO

The PNC Financial Services Group named Christian Winward its new security chief. Winward joined from FirstBank, where he served as CIO and was a member of the senior leadership team. His FirstBank career spanned more than 30 years, beginning as a teller and progressing through leadership roles across technology and project management.

Robert Yox signs on as Lightedge chief information security officer

Lightedge appointed Robert Yox as CISO, bringing over 25 years of technology leadership in cybersecurity, enterprise technology, and risk management. Yox carries deep experience building and maturing security programs across regulated cloud and SaaS environments.

Travelers hires former JetBlue security exec

Travelers appointed Keith Anderson as CISO, bringing over two decades of experience leading cybersecurity organizations across aviation, media, and telecommunications. Anderson previously served as VP and CISO at JetBlue. Before JetBlue, he held cybersecurity leadership roles at WarnerMedia and AT&T.

Assaf Keren takes on Meta CISO role

Meta appointed Assaf Keren as chief information security officer. Keren previously served as SVP and CSO at Qualtrics, where he led enterprise security. Before Qualtrics, he spent nine years at PayPal, holding multiple leadership roles, including CISO.

Coinbase appoints Michael Sikorski as CISO

Coinbase hired Michael Sikorski to be its top security exec. Sikorski joins from Unit 42, where he served as CTO for four years. He brings extensive experience from previous roles at Mandiant, FireEye, and the US National Security Agency.

George Totev takes on CISO role at Clio

Clio appointed George Totev VP of Security and CISO. With 20-plus years of security expertise, Totev brings leadership experience from Goldman Sachs, Visa, Atlassian, and Snowflake. Recently, he served as CISO at Trustero, managing AI security operations and compliance programs.

Tera Ladner promoted to global CISO at Aflac

Aflac promoted Tera Ladner to SVP and Global CISO. Across more than 25 years of leadership, Ladner has built expertise in cybersecurity, information governance, and risk management. Before the promotion, she served as Deputy Global CISO for the insurer. Before joining Aflac, she spent nearly six years at SunTrust Bank as Group VP for Corporate Records & Information Management.

Paul Adams named CISO at Blue Mountain

Blue Mountain appointed Paul Adams as CISO. Adams brings more than 25 years of leadership experience in SaaS and technology spanning enterprise security strategy, security architecture, and cloud infrastructure to the enterprise asset management software maker.

Solana Foundation names Michael Coates as first CISO

The Solana Foundation hired Michael Coates to be its first chief information security officer. Coates brings two decades of cybersecurity leadership, including roles at Mozilla, Twitter, Shape Security, and the OWASP Foundation, and will focus on ecosystem security, malicious uses of AI and crypto-specific threats.

Ravi Thatavarthy joins Primo Brands as CISO

Primo Brands hired Ravi Thatavarthy as chief information security officer to oversee the company’s cybersecurity and IT efforts and strengthen its security and technology foundation. He brings extensive digital security and technology leadership experience across major retail and consumer goods brands.

Datavault AI appoints Barry Childe CISO

Barry Childe, a co-founder of quantum encryption company Arqit, has joined Datavault AI as CISO. Childe previously served as a distinguished engineer at HSBC, and held other senior technology roles at Barclays Capital and VMware.

Jason Cradit joins EverLine as CISO and CTO

Critical infrastructure technical services provider EverLine has hired Jason Cradit as CISO and CTO. Cradit has previously held leadership roles in consulting, software, and infrastructure operations, and founded software vendor Pivvot.

New CISO appointments in June 2026

Drew McCombs named CTO and CISO at Cylerity

Cylerity appointed Drew McCombs as its chief tech and infosec exec. Bringing nearly two decades in healthcare technology, he previously held senior roles at Epic managing mission-critical systems. His expertise includes cloud infrastructure, analytics, AI, and cybersecurity.

John Opala joins Ralph Lauren as CISO

Ralph Lauren appointed John Opala its chief information security officer. Opala previously served at HanesBrands, where he worked with global leadership teams to strengthen cybersecurity capabilities and support enterprise transformation. At Ralph Lauren, he will lead the company’s global cybersecurity strategy, strengthening digital resilience and supporting secure business transformation.

Dave McKenna named CIO and CISO at IDC

IDC appointed Dave McKenna as its chief information and information security exec. McKenna brings deep experience in data architecture, risk management, and cybersecurity leadership across financial services, insurance, and government sectors. Before IDC, he served as VP of Platform Engineering and CISO at Monster.

Infoblox names Henrik Smith CISO

Former Amazon executive Henrik Smith has joined security platform vendor Infoblox as CISO. Smith most recently served as head of security for devices and systems at Amazon, and prior to that was vice-president of security at Salesforce.

GitLab hires Chaim Mazal as CISO

Chaim Mazal, previously chief AI and security officer at Gigamon, has joined GitLab as CISO. He’s been a GitLab customer for over eight years, and moved into the CISO role after serving on the company’s advisory board.

Paras Malhotra joins Starburst as CISO

Enterprise intelligence platform Starburst has hired Paras Malhotra as CISO. He previously served as senior director of information security at Datadog and, prior to that, held a variety of security roles at Amazon Web Services.

Socure hires Mark Carter as CISO

Mark Carter has joined identity infrastructure provider Socure as CISO. He has previously worked as CISO at Navan, Tesla, and Vimeo.

SolarWinds appoints Justin Henkel as CISO

IT management software vendor SolarWinds has named Justin Henkel its new CISO. Henkel was previously deputy CISO at OneTrust, and before that spent 25 years as an intelligence officer in the US Air Force.

Uber taps Philip Martin as security chief

Uber appointed Philip Martin as CISO, strengthening the company’s cybersecurity and digital trust leadership as it continues to expand its global mobility, delivery, and logistics operations.

Ali Waezzadah named CISO at iCOUNTER

iCOUNTER appointed Ali Waezzadah as chief information security officer, a respected cybersecurity executive with more than 20 years of experience leading security transformations across critical infrastructure, media, government, and enterprise environments.

Roger Hale joins 1Kosmos as CISO

1Kosmos appointed Roger Hale as chief information security officer, bringing more than two decades of executive management experience with global cybersecurity companies.

Jacob Berry appointed CISO at Fable Security

Fable Security appointed Jacob Berry as chief information security officer. Berry brings 18 years of experience across technology and cybersecurity, with background in incident response, cyber operations, governance, and compliance to the human risk management vendor.

Novant Health promotes Srini Uppugonduri to CISO

Novant Health promoted cybersecurity leader Srini Uppugonduri to senior vice president and CISO. He brings more than two decades leading enterprise cybersecurity, infrastructure, and technology operations across complex healthcare organizations with expertise in cyber engineering, threat intelligence, and resilience efforts.

US Bank appoints Ann Barron-DiCamillo as global CISO

US Bank appointed Ann Barron-DiCamillo as executive vice president and global chief information security officer. Barron-DiCamillo brings more than 25 years of cybersecurity and risk management experience from roles at Citi, American Express, and as director of the US Computer Emergency Readiness Team.

Texas AG appoints Chad Holmes as CISO

The Texas Office of the Attorney General named Chad Holmes chief information security officer. Holmes brings more than 25 years of private-sector cybersecurity experience, including roles at Legal & General, Kivu Consulting, Optiv, EY, FireEye, Intel, and McAfee, and leads initiatives spanning cybersecurity, AI, cyber resilience, threat intelligence, and incident response readiness.

BreachRx appoints Stephen Garcia as security chief

BreachRx appointed Stephen Garcia as CISO. Garcia brings more than 20 years of security leadership experience, including roles at major financial-services, technology, and enterprise organizations, and will help advance the company’s security strategy and customer trust.

Omnicell promotes Michael McNeil to SVP and CISO

Omnicell promoted Michael McNeil to senior vice president and chief information security officer. The former McKesson CISO will expand his responsibilities to advance Omnicell’s global cybersecurity and cloud security strategy.

Candescent names Thomas Hill as CISO

Candescent appointed Thomas Hill as chief information security officer. Hill brings more than two and a half decades of information security experience, including five years most recently as CISO at nCino and prior service as CIO and CISO at Live Oak Bank.

John Walton appointed CISO at Nubank

Nubank appointed John Walton as chief information security officer. With more than 25 years in security and engineering leadership roles, Walton will lead the digital financial services platform’s information security strategy.

Semperis taps John Podboy as security chief

Semperis appointed John Podboy CISO. Podboy brings more than 15 years of experience spanning cybersecurity, technology management, digital transformation, risk and resilience, including leadership roles at First Citizens Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Thomson Reuters and GE Digital.

Lexitas appoints Joe Giannetti as CIO and CISO

Lexitas named Joe Giannetti its new CIO and CISO. Giannetti brings more than 25 years of experience in technology and security leadership from high-growth organizations, including Employ, Applied Systems, and previous roles managing complex IT infrastructure transformations.

DHS names Supriya Ahuja as acting deputy CISO

The US Department of Homeland Security appointed Supriya Ahuja acting deputy chief information security officer. She brings nearly two decades of cybersecurity and cyber-risk experience across government and private-sector organizations.

Also:

  • William Schmidt named VP & CISO at Pavilion Payments
  • Sean Cassidy joins Plaid as CISO
  • Nic Carroll appointed CISO at Georgia Southern University
  • Michael Kipp promoted to CISO at ChurnZero
  • Tony Arous signs on as Toast’s CISO
  • Ahmed Pasha joins Tradeweb as Global CISO
  • Cyrus Tibbs now CISO of First American
  • Mike Brown appointed CISO at Farmers & Merchants Bank of Long Beach
  • Bryan Thompson now CISO at Luma Financial
  • Randi Kieffer named CISO at USAA

New CISO appointments in May 2026

Backstory names Victor Chang CISO

Backstory, formerly People.ai, has appointed Victor Chang as CISO. Chang has previously served as CISO at Amdocs, among other senior security roles.

Adam Dimopoulos is Entrust’s new CISO

Entrust has appointed former Synchrony VP of Information Security Adam Dimopoulos as its new CISO. Dimopoulos has also previously worked in advisory roles at Microsoft and Gartner.

Tanium names Paul Black as chief information security officer

Tanium appointed Paul Black CISO with a mandate that includes AI-related security priorities. Black brings broad cybersecurity and technology leadership experience across technology, financial-services and enterprise organizations.

Merck appoints Tim McKnight as SVP, IT Risk Management & Security and CISO

Merck has tapped Tim McKnight to head up IT risk management and cybersecurity. He brings more than 30 years of security leadership experience, including senior roles at UnitedHealth Group and SAP and earlier work across major technology, financial-services and government organizations.

Semperis names John Podboy CISO

Semperis appointed John Podboy as chief information security officer. Podboy brings more than 15 years of cybersecurity experience spanning risk, resilience, and digital transformation leadership at Fifth Third Bank, First Citizens Bank, Thomson Reuters, and GE Digital managing security programs across Fortune 100 organizations.

Edwin Ng appointed CISO at LogicGate

LogicGate announced Edwin Ng as chief information security officer. Ng has a two-decade track record of fortifying digital resilience for the world’s most iconic brands.

Also:

  • Erin Heard promoted to acting CISO at USPTO
  • Jason Lee named CISO of PlayOn Sports
  • Alex Burinskiy appointed CISO of Accela
  • Edwin Lopez joins Grupo Vidanta as CISO

New CISO appointments in April 2026

NMFTA appoints Ben Wilkens as cybersecurity director

NMFTA promoted Ben Wilkens to director of cybersecurity. Previously a cybersecurity principal engineer at NMFTA, he brings hands-on transportation experience and advanced cybersecurity expertise. A CISSP, CCSP, and CISM who also holds an active Class A CDL, he will lead NMFTA’s cybersecurity strategy, research, and industry engagement.

Discovery Education appoints Kara Schlageter as first CISO

Discovery Education announced Kara Schlageter as its first chief information security officer. Schlageter brings 25-plus years of cybersecurity, enterprise risk, and large-scale transformation expertise in highly regulated environments. She aligns technical security strategies with business priorities using secure-by-design innovation principles.

Also:

  • Lucas Moody joins Astera Labs as CISO

New CISO appointments in March 2026

Kathy Wang joins micro1 as CISO

Frontier AI model training company micro1 has hired Kathy Wang as CISO. She was most recently CISO at hospitality software developer Otelier, and has previously held top cybersecurity roles at Discord and GitLab.

Green Impact Exchange names John Visneski CISO

John Visneski has joined stock exchange operator Green Impact Exchange as CISO. He was previously CISO at MGM Studios, and following that company’s acquisition by Amazon became head of security for mergers and acquisitions. His cybersecurity career began with the US Air Force, where he served as cyber advisor to the Secretary and Chief of Staff of the Air Force.

US DoW appoints James ‘Aaron’ Bishop deputy CIO and CISO

The US Department of War named James “Aaron” Bishop deputy chief information officer (cybersecurity) and CISO. In the role, he will provide policy, technical, program, and department-wide oversight of cybersecurity matters.

SMBC Americas brings on Donna Hart as CISO

SMBC Americas appointed Donna Hart CISO. Hart brings more than 30 years of experience across information security, infrastructure, and cyber risk management, including leadership experience at Ally Financial and more than 20 years at Wells Fargo and Wachovia.

BayCare taps Robert Carvajal as security chief

BayCare named Robert Carvajal chief information security officer. He will oversee BayCare’s cybersecurity strategy in support of innovation, patient safety, and operational excellence.

Pennsylvania appoints Andy Ritter as CISO

Pennsylvania appoints Andy Ritter as chief information security officer. Ritter brings 30-plus years of cybersecurity and IT experience spanning public and private sectors. Previously serving as deputy CISO, he now leads statewide cyber resilience, enterprise risk management, and security operations.

New CISO appointments in February 2026

Western Alliance appoints Stephen McMaster as CISO

Western Alliance Bank named Stephen McMaster chief information security officer. McMaster brings more than 25 years of experience, including 20 years at Wells Fargo, where he most recently led cloud security, data loss prevention, third-party cybersecurity, and business information security programs.

Teradata names Ken Ricketts as SVP and CISO

Teradata appointed Ken Ricketts senior vice president and chief information security officer. With more than 20 years of experience, he will lead global security strategy with a focus on cloud security, AI-driven innovation, and risk-based governance.

New CISO appointments in January 2026

Julien Mousqueton joins Cohesity as field CISO for Europe

Data security firm Cohesity has hired Julien Mousqueton as field CISO for Europe. His previous role was as CTO at IT service provider Computacenter. He is a reservist advisor for OFAC, the French national police force’s anti-cybercrime division, and created the real-time ransomware activity-tracking platform ransomware.live.

Cook Children’s hires Kathy Jobes as CISO

Cook Children’s Health Care System named Kathy Jobes its chief information security officer. Jobes brings more than 25 years of healthcare cybersecurity experience, with a focus on data governance and risk management, and is known for a human-centric approach to security.

item.title: What the CISO role will look like in 2029
item.description:
Wolfgang Goerlich has spent his career in security and has been a CISO for the past seven years.

Like many long-term security execs, Goerlich has seen plenty of changes within the profession. He’s bracing for more.

“For the future I see growing the role of CISO to be the pacesetter for innovation, to be in the board room and executive conversations advising them on how to take smart, calculated risks with technology, including AI,” says Goerlich, who is now a public sector CISO and a faculty member with IANS Research.

Goerlich sees this as the next step for a role that has continuously evolved since its inception in 1995.

“It’s gone from the ‘department of no’ to ‘let’s slow down’ to ‘let’s take smarter risks based on our understanding of them,’” he adds. “How exciting is this? To be the one to say, ‘You want to take more risk? Let us help you. We can help you make smarter decisions.’”

Goerlich isn’t the only one with such observations. Others similarly believe that the responsibilities assigned to the typical CISO will change in the upcoming years.

Despite a broad consensus on change, predictions vary on how that change will play out in terms of the CISO’s roles and responsibilities. Mirroring the traditional three-year look for strategic planning at many organizations, security leaders see a range of possibilities for the CISO position evolving by 2029. Regardless, all agree that the CISOs of tomorrow will have to work at a faster pace, contend with more threats, and bear more strategic responsibility than they do today.

Research confirms this outlook.

“The CISO role is being redefined in real-time,” states a 2026 KPMG report on the evolving CISO role. “As digital platforms, artificial intelligence (AI), and third-party ecosystems accelerate the pace of change, security leaders are increasingly expected to enable response speed while assuming accountability for enterprise-level risk.”

The report goes on to say, “The modern CISO operates at the crossroads of immense technological opportunity and unprecedented risk. This requires a fundamental evolution of the CISO role itself.”

CISO as ‘strategic facilitator’

KPMG offers ideas on what’s ahead, writing that the future CISO must evolve “from that of a pure technologist to one of a business leader and, critically, a storyteller who can translate complex threats into a business context.” They must become “a strategic facilitator of secure innovation, whose mission is to help the business move at speed in a trusted, safe manner.”

Some CISOs already serve as that strategic facilitator for secure innovation, with researchers and current security chiefs saying they expect a greater percentage of CISO positions to take on that work in the coming years.

Goerlich is experiencing that shift already, having been tasked with standing up an innovation team that includes architecture and engineering professionals as well as security practitioners.

Moreover, his research at IANS has brought him into contact with other CISOs who are leading or co-leading innovation. CEOs and boards increasingly recognize that having security in those leadership roles accelerates — rather than slows — innovation because “security knows how to help them take risks,” he says.

In fact, Goerlich believes more CISOs will have responsibility for enterprise risk in general, in addition to cyber risk, by 2029.

That said, Goerlich doesn’t expect that to be a universal truth. The CISO role will vary from one organization to another in 2029, as it does today, he says, with some more focused on risk and others more tactical.

Security leaders will “self-select into the right organization in ways that fit their temperament, their skills, and their resume,” he says.

‘Enabler of business strategy’

Diana Kelley, CISO at Noma Security, has a similar take on what’s ahead. “The biggest change that is happening is that CISOs are moving more from defender role and compliance to enabler of the business strategy.”

She adds, “It’s becoming more about how to enable the business, how to understand strategically what the business is doing so I can make the business more resilient. It’s already happening. We’ve already seen some CISOs move to being a strategic trust officer and strategic risk partner.”

On the other hand, Kelley also thinks that, thanks in large part to AI, CISOs will need to sharpen their technical chops for the job ahead of them. “I don’t mean CISOs need hands on the keyboard, but they do need to be able to interrogate technically and architecturally what the organization is doing with technology so they can say, ‘This is how we can govern and control this in runtime,’” she explains.

In fact, Kelley suggests that in the future there may be two different types of security leaders in an organization — one focused on shoring up defenses and the other focused on risk and resilience.

Expansion to risk and trust

Longtime security exec Edna Conway also believes the CISO role will continue to morph.

Conway, a former CSO who had CISOs reporting to her, thinks CISOs should expand their responsibilities beyond information security risk to include enterprise risk.

As such, she thinks the title should be chief security and trust officer or chief security and risk officer. She knows something about that: She herself was chief security and risk officer for Azure Infrastructure at Microsoft from 2020 to 2023.

However, Conway, now CEO of EMC Advisors and chief operating and risk officer for TPO Group, isn’t sure all that will happen by 2029.

‘Dynamic environment’ driving CISO evolution

Ali Waezzadah, CISO at iCOUNTER, sees today’s “dynamic environment” — from evolving IT infrastructure to geopolitics to the economy — as driving the next evolution of the position.

More specifically, he sees changing (and increasing) work around managing teams, securing technology, supporting the business direction and strategy, and ensuring compliance with regulatory, security, and governance standards.

The background and experience of security workers is changing, he contends. New technologies are being deployed increasingly faster. Adversaries constantly develop new techniques. The regulatory environment is in flux. And the business itself continues to experiment and revise strategies at shorter intervals. “Those are the things that will force the CISO to adapt,” he adds.

All that is regularly reshaping both the day-to-day actions of the CISO and the remit that falls under the title. That, in turn, is forcing security leaders to be more agile than ever before, Waezzadah says.

“By 2029 they’ll have more things they’ll have to pay attention to,” he predicts. “How and what CISOs have to protect is rapidly changing, and they have to be much more prepared for a dynamic landscape. They need to be more nimble and flexible.”

‘Strategic architect of business outcomes’

Of course, change is not new to CISOs as they’ve seen their mandate expand over the past decades, says John White, field CISO for security tech company Torq.

The upcoming years will require CISOs to build and manage an operation that can move at lightning speed, a consequence of AI’s use by the organization and its adversaries, White says. To do that, CISOs must build and manage a new type of security department, one where agents execute and human workers define and oversee outcomes.

“The traditional security model we’re used to is no longer going to be sufficient for what’s upon us, and the CISO role will evolve to be a more agile, product-oriented role and to be someone who can pull holistic teams together quickly to engineer responses,” he says, adding that CISOs will need strong risk skills and business acumen to do all that.

In an online post, he writes “The CISO of the near future is less a chief technologist and more a strategic architect of business outcomes, designing human-machine teams that reimagine the target operating model in response to both risk and opportunity.”

CISO as orchestrator

Andrew Obadiaru, CISO at Cobalt, a security services company, also believes “by 2029 the CISO will be even more of a business leader than a technical leader.”

“Security will increasingly be measured by how quickly organizations can identify, validate, and reduce risk,” he says. “The CISO will be responsible for enabling the business to adopt AI safely, managing software supply chain risk, and ensuring the organization can continuously validate its security posture in an environment where attackers are operating at machine speed.”

As a result, Obadiaru sees the CISO role becoming “less about owning security technology and more about orchestrating security across engineering, IT, product, legal, procurement, and the executive team.”

He expects three main priorities to dominate the role in the future: continuously validating organizational exposure rather than relying on assessments; ensuring AI is adopted securely across the enterprise; and accelerating remediation.

CISOs will have to act faster, too. “As a result, CISOs will spend less time reviewing individual technical findings and more time building automated decision-making processes, resilient engineering practices, and governance models that allow organizations to respond safely at machine speed,” Obadiaru says.

And they’ll have to change their operating model. “Security has always been about managing uncertainty. What’s changing is the speed at which uncertainty develops,” he says. “AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, software development, and attacker innovation simultaneously. That means the CISO must evolve from managing security programs to managing adaptive security systems.”

However, he believes the fundamental mission will stay the same.

“The CISO’s responsibility is still to protect the organization’s ability to operate by understanding risk, communicating it effectively, and helping the business make informed decisions,” he adds. “Technology evolves, but leadership, trust, sound judgment, and clear communication remain constant requirements.”
